scope.method: Independent artifact-only mechanical and semantic audit; no source fetch was required because material conflicts were classifiable from the supplied artifacts.

qa_checks.observed: The 186 Phase 3 stable IDs reconcile one-to-one with the union of the four regional Phase 2 sets; no duplicate ID occurs in either set.
No exact normalized alias duplicate was demonstrated. Six exact city/county/state collision groups exist, but the artifacts identify different owners or projects and do not prove duplicate records.

All 513 Phase 3 action primary URLs and all 452 present project source URLs are syntactically valid HTTPS/HTTP URLs; all 513 action URLs and all 186 project IDs are present in the corresponding Phase 3 Markdown.

The reviewed records generally distinguish withdrawal, moratorium, referral, utility proceedings, company announcements, tax incentives, and groundbreaking from government approval, construction completion, or energization. No demonstrated company/reporting milestone was mislabeled as a government action. Keep these distinctions in final rendering.

anchors.example: GA-005 withdrawal is not current approval
utility approval and company groundbreaking are separated from permit/energization
FERC co-location rejection is not campus denial

anchors.claim: evidence-backed 2024–2030 Gantt chart
7 observed projects and 20 milestones
schema exists but does not provide bars/crosswalks for the 186 Phase 3 projects

conflicting_claims: The brief scopes the public-project deliverable to a 2024–2030 Gantt.
The only machine-readable construction-cycle schedule covers seven benchmark projects, not the 186 accepted Phase 3 county-pair projects; no stable-ID crosswalk or all-project schedule is supplied.
findings.safest_resolution: Do not label the current schedule as a comprehensive project Gantt. Either build evidence-backed bars/crosswalks for the accepted projects or explicitly label the output as seven observed benchmark schedules and disclose that county-project coverage is absent.

anchors.claim: null date with undated_web_page precision
null date with undated_register_entry precision
null date with undated_register_entry precision
null action_date but date_text April 2026
null action_date for an undated accessed page
ISO dates have no precision field

conflicting_claims: Phase 3 metadata describes date validation, but 150 of 513 actions omit date_precision, four use non-enum custom values, and 11 are null or explicitly undated.
Month-only and undated evidence is mixed into action records without a uniform precision enum, which can make a Gantt imply day-level certainty.
findings.safest_resolution: Normalize precision mechanically to the stated evidence: day/month/year/undated; retain date_text for month-only or accessed-page records and never invent a day. Treat missing precision as unknown until normalized.

anchors.claim: allowed date_precision/status/certainty/basis enums
24 enum violations across 20 milestones; evidence_note absent on all 20
missing dates should remain null and must not be invented

conflicting_claims: The schema permits date_precision day/month/season/year/unknown, status actual/forecast/announced/complete/cancelled/unknown, and basis observed/official_forecast/planning_range/inference/announcement_only.

Observed rows use values such as official_release, developer_release, forecast_at_source_date, actual_statement, announcement, month_start_approximation, month_end_approximation, and year_end, and omit required evidence_note.
findings.safest_resolution: Map source labels to the declared enum without changing factual meaning, preserve the original label in an evidence note, and use null/unknown where mapping would overstate precision.

anchors.claim: tier values are strings T1–T5
tier values are numeric 1–5
Phase 3 has no per-source tier attached to these URLs

conflicting_claims: The four regional Phase 2 sets contain 356 source records with T1–T5 coverage, but the field type is inconsistent across regions.
Phase 3 action and project URLs are not linked to source tiers, so a final source-domain/tier mix cannot be reproduced from the accepted action set.
findings.safest_resolution: Normalize tier values to one representation and preserve source IDs/URLs when carrying evidence into Phase 3; report the current tier mix as Phase 2-only, not as a Phase 3 action-evidence mix.

anchors.claim: 19 project rows have no project-level source_urls field
19 project rows have no project-level source_urls field

conflicting_claims: Phase 3 requires project-level source URL coverage for most county-pair files and achieves 452 URLs overall.

The Ohio/Indiana and Pennsylvania/New Jersey/New York/Washington files rely on action-level URLs only, reducing schema uniformity and making row-level source aggregation non-equivalent across the 186 projects.
findings.safest_resolution: Retain and expose each action primary_url, but add a derived project-level source list before claiming uniform source coverage; do not treat the missing field as absence of evidence.

anchors.claim: government_inspection is dated 2026-03-19 while source date is 2025-03-19
Phase 2 milestone 2026-03-19 is unsupported; official release is 2025-03-19
inspection action dated 2025-03-19

conflicting_claims: Phase 2 records an inspection on 2026-03-19.
Phase 3’s official-source review records the inspection/release on 2025-03-19 and explicitly identifies the Phase 2 date as a data-entry error.
findings.safest_resolution: Use 2025-03-19 for the inspection and remove the unsupported 2026-03-19 duplicate; retain the correction note in provenance.

anchors.claim: TDLR registration TABS2026024088 starts 2025-10-30 and completes 2027-04-19
Oracle 1H27 delivery and TDLR April 19, 2027 are different milestones
TDLR registration TABS2026024110 starts 2026-09-04 and completes 2028-04-18; future estimate, not a local building permit

conflicting_claims: The Phase 1 Frontier record presents a 2025–2027 TDLR registration and Oracle’s 1H27 delivery statement.
The Phase 3 Texas record presents a separate 2026–2028 TDLR registration and says physical construction/first-building status is incomplete. The artifacts do not provide an address/phase crosswalk.
findings.safest_resolution: Keep the two TDLR registrations as separate candidate phases/buildings until an owner/address crosswalk is established; do not merge them into one 2025–2028 bar or treat registration completion as energization.

anchors.claim: reported_mw null; $1.9B and 2.1M square feet supported; seed 1.9 GW not supported
regional ID is locally approved but has no completion/energization

conflicting_claims: The national seed uses 1,900 MW for an EdgeCore Mesa expansion ID.
The regional and county evidence use a different stable ID and support $1.9B/2.1M square feet, not 1.9 GW.
findings.safest_resolution: Keep MW null for the accepted regional project, preserve $1.9B as investment, and resolve the national-to-regional ID crosswalk before aggregating; never convert dollars or square footage into MW.

anchors.claim: under construction per tracker
100 MW phase plus 82.5 MW follow-on, with staged 2026/2027 targets
state release supports 100 MW/70 MW critical IT; no energization or CO

conflicting_claims: The seed tracker reports 1,500 MW and under construction.
The regional/county evidence supports a 100 MW first phase and 82.5 MW follow-on, with no completion or energization finding.
findings.safest_resolution: Render 100 MW as the evidenced phase and 82.5 MW as a separate target/follow-on; retain 1,500 MW only as an unverified tracker lead and do not label it live or committed.

anchors.claim: Joule 455 MW Phase 1 under construction; 4,000+ MW full buildout proposed; tracker incorrectly says 4 GW under construction
Creekstone 220 MW Phase 1 under construction; 2 GW tracker and 9,700+ MW expansion are different scopes
Phase 1 status is separated from proposed full buildout and no power-on/final CUP is verified

conflicting_claims: Tracker/seed-scale values can be read as 4 GW and 2 GW under construction.
Government inventory and county review distinguish 455 MW and 220 MW Phase 1 scopes from 4,000+ MW and 9,700+ MW proposed expansions.
findings.safest_resolution: Use separate phase and ultimate-buildout fields; chart only the evidenced Phase 1 construction status and label full-campus values as proposed. Do not sum or substitute tracker-scale values.

anchors.claim: five-building expansion

four single-story data-center buildings plus support buildings
same four-versus-five discrepancy

Phase 3 county findings enumerate four data-center buildings plus support structures and identify the five-building description as inconsistent.
findings.safest_resolution: Use the county-approved description—four data-center buildings plus support structures—for government-scope reporting; retain five only as an attributed Phase 2 shorthand if its source definition is shown.

Anthem row may be an alias/misattribution; resolve before separate counting
both IDs are accepted records in the same Tulsa location

The separate Anthem record carries an unverified 800 MW trade figure and no primary record, while warning it may be the same project.

anchors.claim: Related/CoreWeave up to 302 MW; Project Jade overlap requires parcel crosswalk
Project Jade 2,700 MW may overlap with Related/CoreWeave
Related is kept separate pending parcel crosswalk
negative search only; do not merge with Related Digital/CoreWeave

The other is Google/Jupiter Star Project Jade/Tembo at 2,700 MW with unresolved parcel/developer identity; the same-county location does not establish two independent campuses.
findings.safest_resolution: Keep records separate for provenance but flag the identity as unresolved; do not sum 302 MW and 2,700 MW or infer construction status for Project Jade from the Related record until parcel evidence is available.

anchors.claim: Tripletail 7,000 MW ultimate scale; not current load
Pole Canyon/Pony 1,820 MW proposed; possible overlap with Tripletail
both accepted as proposed leads; no parcel crosswalk resolves overlap

conflicting_claims: Tripletail and Pole Canyon/Pony have separate stable IDs and reported capacities of 7,000 MW ultimate and 1,820 MW proposed.
Phase 2 explicitly says the staff-report layout and seed names create possible overlap and prohibits summing without a parcel crosswalk.
findings.safest_resolution: Do not aggregate the two capacity figures or render them as independent campuses; preserve the overlap warning until parcel and case identifiers are cross-walked.
